evidence_notes: Claim (Venus is too dangerous to live on / people would die) surfaces only in para 3-4; support is source facts (97% carbon dioxide, corrosive sulfuric acid clouds, heat wiping out past oceans/wildlife); para 2 (Mars, NASA, orbital speeds) bears on nothing. org 3 (controlling idea stated but buried mid-essay; opening gives no orientation and the Mars/orbits part is a digression); dev 3 (specific source facts present but one sentence lifted near-verbatim - patchwriting caps here - and support is listed more than explained); conv 3 (duplicated phrases, 'acid in acid in', 'carbon dioixde', 'Too see', unclear 'so they could live'; meaning recoverable but re-read to repair); arg 3 (position committed by the end but reasons are asserted from the source, never shown; last two parts circle the same danger claim).

Claim is an unnamed 'This is right' endorsement of the emotion-reading technology; support is the 83/9/6/2 percent figures and a quoted line about Dr. Huang's team, then a long riff that the world will have no violence and 'dreams come true'. org 3 (controlling idea stated as 'the main point is...' but the essay opens mid-argument with no orientation and ends in a run-on with no closing; the utopian stretch does not relate); dev 3 (percentages and a named authority are specific, but they are dropped in and the reader supplies the link; the sweeping peace claims get no support at all); conv 3 (gald, workd, pefrom, beacuse, xepress, 'the person feel', 60-word run-on; errors accumulate and force re-reading, never guessing); arg 3 (position committed and enthusiastic but reasons are asserted and escalate into restatement rather than showing why).

Claim: self-driving cars would help a lot / are a great idea. Reasons: fewer wrecks from bad drivers, a drunk-driver scenario reasoned out ('since you cant do it yourself because your not in the right stae of mind'), road rebuilding costs too much, manufacturers profit, plus a text-based point about liability law. org 3 (thesis early and held, frame present, but the third part drifts from road costs to profits to hovercraft and never returns); dev 4 (drunk-driving scenario is a realized example and its connection to safety is stated, though most other support is general assertion); conv 3 (wreacks/wreaks, 'your drunk', 'stae', 'beheld responcibale', no sentence capitalization; errors accumulate and the law sentence needs a repair re-read); arg 4 (one reason genuinely reasoned - human impairment removed by the computer - but no opposing view answered and the conclusion is exactly what the prompt implies).

Persona letter from Luke Bomberger urging readers to join the UNRRA as Seagoing Cowboys; two reasons - helping war-devastated families and seeing the world (Acropolis, gondola in Venice, excavated castle in Crete, Panama Canal). org 4 (thesis early, opening and closing both present, all parts on-claim, but the help-others and see-the-world halves are announced as parallel and swap freely); dev 4 (named landmarks are specific and their connection to joining is stated - 'Don't tell me you wouldn't love... All you have to do is join' - but the helping half stays general and explanation is restatement); conv 4 (devestated, expirience, appriciative, contibute recur, but sentence shapes vary purposefully - questions, imperatives, short beats - and nothing needs repair; repeated misspellings stop rung 5); arg 4 (one reason reasoned via the reciprocity appeal 'wouldn't you want someone to help you', but no opposing view, no qualification, conclusion is what the prompt implies).

Claim: the Facial Action Coding System is valuable because it can detect emotions students hide and let lessons adapt; support is two quotes from D'Alto (trouble describing facial traits; a classroom computer noticing confusion and modifying the lesson) plus general claims that students don't ask for help. org 4 (thesis at end of the opening and held, frame present, all parts on-claim, but the problem/solution/elaboration parts function as interchangeable supports); dev 4 (quotes are specific and the connection is stated - 'This shows that...' - but the explanation restates the quote and several claims rest on general assertion); conv 3 (indivuals, mordern, diffucult, insturctor, benefical, 'Teachers a very educated', and 'By being said the students that can't comprehend the lesson... that they can to so' forces a repair re-read; errors accumulate); arg 4 (one reason reasoned - bettering something you partly know beats work you have no knowledge of - but no opposing view and the verdict is what the prompt implies).

No argumentative claim beyond 'The Challenge of Exploring Venus is a informative text'; body is First/Secondly/Lastly summary of source facts (800 degrees, 90x pressure, light cannot penetrate the atmosphere, silicon electronics), with a stray drift into the 1800s and World War II. org 3 (a controlling idea of sorts is stated and signposted parts exist, but the last body part loses its job mid-unit and the conclusion stops rather than closes); dev 3 (figures are specific but the passage is stitched source phrasing with little transformation - patchwriting caps here - and nothing is put to work for a claim); conv 2 (the sumfor, 'The scientifict However, peering', 'this things starts doo do about 1800's', 'they can move this things fon computer' - at least once I must guess the intent, not repair it); arg 2 (the position is a vague characterization of the text handed back, with summary in place of reasons).

Claim: limiting car usage has advantages - less pollution, more activity, saved money. Support is heavily quoted from 'Car-Free Cities' (12%/50% emissions, Vauban's 5,500 residents, Bogota's 118 miles of bike paths, parks and rebuilt sidewalks), each quote tagged with 'This meaning' or 'This being said'. org 4 (thesis early and held, frame present, all parts on-claim, but the Vauban and Bogota blocks are parallel exhibits that swap freely and partly repeat); dev 4 (support specific throughout and a connection stated for nearly every quote, but the explanations mostly restate the quote and the quotes sit alongside rather than inside the writer's sentences); conv 3 (advantanges, respondible, bicylce, 'there is advantages', repeated 'This meaning' fragments, comma splices; 'some places in the United states gases are half of the areas pollution' needs a repair re-read); arg 4 (one reason reasoned - walkable suburbs remove the drive and therefore the gas cost - but no opposing view, no qualification, conclusion is the prompt's own framing).

Opens 'The challege of exploring Venus is not a great idea' and immediately follows with a borrowed sentence saying studying Venus is worthy; support is source material on 90x pressure and hottest surface temperature, then a final part on scientists floating safely at 170 degrees that undercuts the stated position. org 2 (the controlling idea is contradicted in the adjacent sentence, there is no closing at all, and the last part bears no recoverable relation to the claim); dev 3 (one specific supported point - pressure/heat quote glossed 'This shows that Venus is not a safe planet' - but the material is stitched source phrasing and the plentiful-solar-power line argues against the claim it is attached to); conv 3 ('are been send', 'Studying Venus is a worthy because', 'Venus is simple see', 'conditions on surface Venus allow scientists to float'; meaning recoverable but repeatedly needs repair); arg 3 (position stated with commitment and repeated, but held inconsistently and every reason is asserted - 'This shows that' - never shown).

Claim: emotion-reading technology in classrooms is valuable, for three announced reasons - lessons suited to the student, heading off anger/stress, making students feel valued; the only borrowed support is the article's point that the computer tailors lessons to shown emotions, the rest is the writer's own reasoning about what the FACS 'could' do. org 4 (thesis early and held, frame present, three body parts map one-to-one onto the announced reasons and would swap without loss); dev 4 (the tailoring capability is a concrete particular and its connection is stated - students don't seek help, so automatic detection fills the gap - but most support is general assertion, not specific throughout); conv 4 (acknowleding, attendence, 'each students needs', a comma splice and a parallelism slip in longer sentences; errors visible, nothing needs repair, but control wavers so rung 5 fails); arg 4 (reasons genuinely reasoned but no opposing consideration, no qualification, and the verdict is exactly what the prompt implies).

Claim, stated at the body's start and again at the end: the author supported his idea that studying Venus is a worthy pursuit despite the dangers. Part one paraphrases the dangers in the writer's own words (97 percent carbon dioxide, 800 degrees, 90x pressure); part two lists three attributed quotes - astronomers fascinated, Earth-like surface features, silicon carbide lasting three weeks. org 4 (dangers-then-reasons frame with the idea held and all parts on-claim, but the three quoted supports inside the body swap freely and the closing only restates); dev 4 (support specific and each quote framed by a sentence stating what it is doing, but every gloss restates the quote and the quotes sit alongside the writer's sentences); conv 4 (Althrough, 'Although, the conditions are extreme.' fragment, 'the atmosphere high', fetures, 'a Earth-like'; errors visible, nothing needs repair, but formulaic 'The author states' patterning blocks rung 5); arg 3 (position is essentially the prompt's own wording affirmed, and the essay never says why the author's reasons are good - it reports them and circles back).
